Your products may already be listed on AEC Integrations. Free lets you keep that listing accurate. Managed lets you tell the full story: how teams use each product, which trades and phases it serves, and which data flows you confirm.

<!-- docs:plans-actions -->

<!-- docs:plans-comparison -->

## What every plan includes

On Free and on Managed, anyone with a seat can:

- keep your company details current: the description, website, headquarters, logo and contact links,
- keep each product's description, website, logo and categories current,
- claim and maintain the integrations your company builds, add your own links, and request a change to a detail on one you do not own,
- invite colleagues and manage seats. See [Your seat](/docs/vendors/your-seat),
- work through the company and product checklists. See [Your checklists](/docs/vendors/checklists).

[Editing your profile and products](/docs/vendors/editing-profile-and-products) lists every field and how it saves.

The company name and the product names are not edited in the portal.

The product details on this list are the ones that feed search ranking. They are editable on Free for that reason. [How ranking works](/docs/trust/how-ranking-works) explains how they count.

## What Managed adds

- **How teams use it.** Show buyers, in your own words, what your product does on a real project.
- **Trades, audiences and phases.** Set the trades, audiences and project phases each product serves, so its listing describes it accurately.
- **Integrations page and API docs links.** Send evaluators straight from your listing to your docs. They show under **Resources** on your product page.
- **Confirmed data flows.** Say which data moves in each of your integrations. Your answer counts toward the integration's agreement label, the same as your partner's. See [Confirming integration data](/docs/vendors/confirming-integration-data).
- **Connector integrations.** Claim, edit, retire and restore the integrations you deliver through a connector, not only the ones you built directly. See [Owning an integration](/docs/vendors/owning-an-integration).
- **Review replies.** Answer reviews of your products in public, so buyers see your side. We check each reply before it goes live. See [Replying to reviews](/docs/vendors/replying-to-reviews).
- **Search engine notice.** We tell search engines each time you update a public page.

On Free, your edits still go live straight away, and search engines find them on their own schedule through our sitemap. Telling a search engine about a page does not decide whether it crawls, indexes or ranks that page. The search engine decides that.

On a Free product, the Managed fields stay visible in the portal. They are read-only, and each one says it is part of Managed.

## Why buyers trust the order

Every listing is sorted the same way: how well it matches the search, then how complete it is. Your plan is not part of that. Neither is anything else you pay for.

Your plan also never decides:

- whether a review is published or removed,
- whether a listing exists,
- how an agreement label is worked out. Both companies' answers count the same.

Each plan panel in your portal says the same: "No plan changes where you rank or appear, or whether a review is published." [How ranking works](/docs/trust/how-ranking-works) sets out the full rule and how we check it.

## When a Managed plan ends

This applies to a pilot too.

- Your company moves to Free. Your seats, sign-in and portal stay.
- Nothing you entered is removed. Your listings stay published.
- The portal shows a banner with the date the plan ended. It lists what still works and what is now read-only.
- Everything in "What every plan includes" keeps working, the checklists included.
- Everything in "What Managed adds" becomes read-only.
- We stop telling search engines about your changes. Your edits still go live.
- You can no longer write, edit or resubmit a reply to a review. Published replies stay up, and you can still withdraw one.
- An integration delivered through a connector that you already claimed stays claimed. One you retired stays retired. Open change requests on one move to AEC Integrations.
- Each product's checklist counts three steps again, as on Free. See [Your checklists](/docs/vendors/checklists).

## Getting Managed

Managed is priced per product. Tell us which products you want on Managed, and we set it up with you. The plan panel in your portal shows your company's price. We bill paid plans by invoice or purchase order. Free plans require neither.

<!-- docs:plans-cta -->

To start, claim your listing. The claim form asks which plan you are interested in, Free, Managed or not sure yet, and we confirm the plan with you before anything is billed. When we approve a claim, we put your company on Free or on Managed, and the approval email tells you which. See [Claiming your vendor listing](/docs/vendors/claiming-your-listing). If your company is already on Managed, a new seat does not change that.

The plan renews for another year unless you opt out before the renewal date. At least 30 days before that date, we send you the renewal price and date in writing. A price change needs your agreement. We never take silence as agreement.

The portal shows your plan's status, and the end date where there is one. Before the end date, everyone with a seat and AEC Integrations get an email. Nothing changes before that date. A Managed plan does not lapse on its own. Its status changes only when we act on it. To opt out of renewal, or to change anything about billing, [contact us](/contact).

### Can we cancel a Managed plan early?

The term runs to the end of the paid year. If you opt out of renewal, you keep Managed through the current year, and we issue no further invoices.
